green adjective

also bright green, grass green, emerald green, olive green, sea green, very green, be green, become green

classical

Traupman 115
Traupman 117
Traupman 251

viridis, viride

Other words

  • prasinus, prasina, prasinum — leek-green

    also used · classical · Petr. 27; Plin. NH 37.181; Mart. 10.29.4 (Lewis & Short); Andresian p. 50; Traupman 251: bright grass green

    Greek πράσινος, from πράσον, a leek: a full green, the colour of the Greens in the circus (factiō prasina, Suet. Cal. 55; Lewis & Short). Andresian uses it for a full green and viridis for a light one.

  • herbāceus, herbācea, herbāceum — grass-green

    also used · classical · Plin. NH 19.110 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 251

  • smaragdinus, smaragdina, smaragdinum — emerald green

    also used · classical · Lewis & Short: “of the emerald”; Traupman 251

  • olīvāceus, olīvācea, olīvāceum — olive green

    also used · modern · Traupman 251

    Not in Lewis & Short.

  • glaucus, glauca, glaucum — greyish green, sea-green

    also used · classical · Lewis & Short: “bright, sparkling, grayish”, poetic and post-Augustan; Traupman 251

  • perviridis, perviride — very green

    also used · classical · Plin. NH 6.87: color (Lewis & Short); Traupman 251

  • vireō, virēre, viruī — be green (of leaves)

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 5.37: alia semper virent (Lewis & Short); Traupman 251

  • virēscō, virēscere — turn green

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Verg. G. 1.55: grāmina (Lewis & Short); Traupman 251

See also colour.
